<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Install the client, open a practice connection, and check both package versions.
</div>

This chapter creates the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection.
Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed
with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

## Before you start

You need R 4.1 or newer and internet access for installation and the practice
data download. The lessons use a local DSLite practice server. RStudio is a convenient editor; ordinary R also works. Download the book helpers below; you do not need a Git checkout.

Run this **installation block once**, before the examples. It installs every
package needed by the client, the local practice server and the helpers.


``` r
install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal", "DSLite", "DBI", "RSQLite",
                   "resourcer", "withr", "openssl", "jsonlite", "knitr",
                   "rmarkdown", "duckdb", "lme4"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBase@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOP@2.10.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.5", upgrade = "never")
```

The *client* is the package on your computer. The *server* runs requests near the
data; DSLite lets you run it locally for practice. Record the installed versions with your study, as shown in
[Checking and recording a study](book-17-reproduce.html).

## Get the book helpers

The book helpers are distributed separately from the package.
Download [book-helpers.zip](../downloads/book-helpers.zip) from this site, leaving
it zipped in your Downloads folder. In R, run this block and select that ZIP
when the file chooser opens:

```r
book_dir <- path.expand("~/book-work")
dir.create(book_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
unzip(file.choose(), exdir = book_dir)
setwd(book_dir)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path("tools/book",
  c("practice.R", "fixture.R", "connection.R", "display.R", "load-practice.R", "load-numeric.R", "case-helpers.R")))),
  file.exists("tools/book/capstone.R"))
getwd()
```

The last line prints your home directory followed by `/book-work`. In every new
R session run `setwd(path.expand("~/book-work"))` before the chapter setup.
The ZIP preserves `tools/book/` automatically. Alternatively, save the individual
[practice](../downloads/practice.R), [fixture](../downloads/fixture.R),
[connection](../downloads/connection.R), [display](../downloads/display.R) and
[practice loader](../downloads/load-practice.R) and
[numeric loader](../downloads/load-numeric.R) and
[formula helpers](../downloads/case-helpers.R) files under `book-work/tools/book/`.
Keep the numeric loader filename `load-numeric.R`; the practice loader sources it.
Save the [capstone helper](../downloads/capstone.R) in `book-work/tools/book/`;
chapter 18's solution uses it.

`display.R` formats released summaries, tables and returned symbol mappings for reading. It does not
retrieve patient rows. `practice.R` defines the local practice server.
`connection.R` defines `book_connect()`, which reads the connection settings and
attaches the selected resource. Source these downloaded files in the order shown in each chapter.

Leave `connection.R` at its defaults for local practice. The
[Opal connection chunk](#connect-to-your-opal-server) below replaces those defaults
for a session on your study server.

## Check the client


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
vapply(c("dsOMOPClient", "dsOMOP", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(package) as.character(packageVersion(package)), character(1))
```

```
#> dsOMOPClient       dsOMOP          DSI       DSLite dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.5"     "2.10.5"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"
```

``` r
ds.omop.client.version()
```

```
#> [1] "2.10.5"
```

This reports the package on your computer. A correct client version alone does not
prove that the server has the matching methods.

## Load two public synthetic datasets

The practice server has two resources. **GiBleed** supports the introductory
schema and vocabulary lessons. **Synthea27Nj** supplies hemoglobin and other
numeric measurements with units for [Working with lab values](book-14-labs.html). Both contain fictional patients; “numeric”
means populated numeric fields, not real patient records. GiBleed has 44,053
measurement rows but no populated `value_as_number`, so it cannot teach lab-value
reducers on its own.

The local practice loader is [tools/book/load-practice.R](../downloads/load-practice.R).
It downloads the two [Eunomia datasets](https://github.com/OHDSI/EunomiaDatasets)
and creates the SQLite databases used by the lessons. Run it once from `book-work`:

```r
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        c("tools/book/load-practice.R", "../practice-data"))
stopifnot(file.exists("../practice-data/gibleed.sqlite"),
          file.exists("../practice-data/numeric.sqlite"))
```

It uses the installed DBI, RSQLite, duckdb, withr, openssl and jsonlite packages. The source data are Apache-2.0 licensed;
keep their [license](https://github.com/OHDSI/EunomiaDatasets/blob/3d349dcdd79cc346b8e36eb837e49feffe7f7497/LICENSE)
with redistributed copies. 

<div class="book-note">
**Note**

The categorical, date and mortality lessons also use a small **synthetic
questionnaire dataset**, created temporarily by `fixture.R`. It contains education,
fever, visits and causes of death, including missing answers and partial birth dates.
Its category and formula exercises add clearly labelled synthetic vocabulary
relationships and standardized creatinine inputs.
It is separate from the two practice resources; each chapter identifies its dataset.
</div>

## Open the practice server

Use `book-work` as your R working directory after running the installation block above. DSLite executes real DataSHIELD methods inside R;
this helper creates one server with both loaded resources and attaches GiBleed.


``` r
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"
```

`conns` holds connections, not patient rows. The other resource is named `numeric`.
Every chapter includes its complete fresh-session setup, including assigning
`conns <- practice$conns`. Numeric chapters select `"numeric"` through the same
configuration. Questionnaire chapters source `fixture.R` and call
`practice <- book_fixture()` before assigning `conns`; this is always local DSLite.

## Check the server


``` r
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)[c("server", "published", "running", "ready")]
```

```
#>   server published running ready
#> 1   site    2.10.5  2.10.5  TRUE
```

The reply comes from the server. `ready` confirms that the running package and
the methods available to your session agree.

## Connect to your Opal server

Your administrator has already set up the server and gives you its URL, your user
and password (or token), the resource names and the DataSHIELD profile. Use those
details in this connection chunk.

In a fresh session, replace the chapter's local connection chunk with the block
below. It is not executed here: the printed chapter results use the local
practice data. Use `"numeric"` instead of `"gibleed"` in the final attach call for
a numeric-data chapter; the analysis code that follows the connection is the same.


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
library(DSOpal)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R", local = TRUE)
source("tools/book/practice.R")
book_driver <- "Opal"
opal_url <- "<server-url>"
opal_project <- "<project>"
opal_resources <- c(gibleed = "<gibleed-resource>", numeric = "<numeric-resource>")
opal_profile <- "<profile>"
resource_names <- book_resource_names(book_driver, opal_project, opal_resources)
Sys.setenv(BOOK_OPAL_USER = "<user>", BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD = "<password>")
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(server = "site", url = opal_url,
  user = Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_USER"), password = Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD"),
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = opal_profile)
conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = FALSE)
ds.omop.connect(resource = resource_names[["gibleed"]], conns = conns)
practice <- list(conns = conns, path = character())
names(conns)
```

Keep credentials in your private R session, outside shared study scripts. If you
receive an access token, set `Sys.setenv(BOOK_OPAL_TOKEN = "<token>")` instead
of the user and password, and replace the builder's `user` and `password`
arguments with `token = Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_TOKEN")`. Later calls to
`book_connect()` use the same token. Resource names include their project prefix, for example
`study.measurements`; enter the project and resource parts separately above.
The two names in `opal_resources` map the book's datasets to the resources you
were given. Your study data will produce different results from the practice data.

[Chapter 2](book-02-connect.html) explains attaching resources and switching
between them. Chapters that introduce the synthetic questionnaire or a local
two-site example identify that practice setup explicitly.


``` r
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)[c("server", "published", "running", "ready")]
```

## Exercise 2: a common variant

Which packages run locally?

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
vapply(c("DSI", "DSLite", "dsOMOPClient"), function(x) as.character(packageVersion(x)), "")
```

```
#>          DSI       DSLite dsOMOPClient 
#>      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"     "2.10.5"
```

DSI and dsOMOPClient handle analyst requests. DSLite runs the practice server
locally, using the dsOMOP and dsBase packages installed in the same block.

</details>

## Exercise 3: a pitfall to avoid

Check that the shared resource configuration names both practice datasets.

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
source("tools/book/connection.R")
resource_names
```

```
#>   gibleed   numeric 
#> "gibleed" "numeric"
```

These names select the two local practice datasets. The Opal connection chunk
replaces them with the resource names supplied by your administrator.

</details>
## Recap

You can distinguish your client installation from the server installation and have a practice connection.
